persona.who: 22, wants to be a filmmaker, father is a government doctor who wants him to do MBBS or at least MBA. Fights every dinner.
persona.note: papa says films are for rich kids and I should do MBA. we fight every night. I love him and I also feel like he doesn't see me at all. mummy cries in the kitchen

understanding.bridge: The fight every night is what the Gita calls wanting your own way and then being angry when it does not happen. The love is real, but the wanting is what keeps it burning.
understanding.week_thesis: Seven days from fighting the one you love most to seeing that the love and the fight are two different things, and that you can hold both.

week_beats.hook: You recognise the night fight and the love that makes it hurt more than it should.
week_beats.diagnose: You see that the fight is not about films or an MBA. It is about needing his approval to feel your own path is real.
week_beats.steady: You hold that what is yours cannot be taken by what he says, and that his approval is not the measure of your worth.
week_beats.act: You try one conversation where you speak your truth and ask to be seen, without trying to win him over.
week_beats.story: A son who stood before his father and asked to be seen shows you what it looks like when the night ends.

understanding.core_struggle: A son who loves his father but fights every night over his future, feeling the man he loves does not see him at all.
understanding.mirror: Mummy cries in the kitchen, and you are caught between the two people who made you.
understanding.insight: It isn't the task that weighs on you. It's waiting for someone else to tell you it was enough.

queries.hook: The pain of fighting the parent you love most, and the fear that they do not see who you are.
queries.diagnose: When your worth depends on a parent's approval, every word of blame shakes you; craving their approval keeps the mind unsteady and the night alive.
queries.steady: Praise and blame come and go, and the self that is yours does not rise or fall with them; what is yours cannot be taken by what they say.
queries.act: Speak your truth to your father, not to win the argument, but to be seen; and hold your own ground on what you want to become.
queries.story: A son who stood before his father and asked to be seen, and found that being seen was the only thing that could end the night.

verse.speaker: Arjuna
verse.setting: Arjuna, seeing his own family in the enemy ranks, collapses in grief before the battle.
verse.sanskrit: सीदन्ति मम गात्राणि मुखं च परिशुष्यति । वेपथुश्च शरीरे मे रोमहर्षश्च जायते ॥ गाण्डीवं स्रंसते हस्तात्त्वक्चैव परिदह्यते । न च शक्नोम्यवस्थातुं भ्रमतीव च मे मनः ॥
verse.line: Shaking limbs, a dry mouth, a racing body: the Gita opens with a panic attack, not a hero.
verse.translation: My limbs give way, my mouth is parched, my body trembles and my hair stands on end.
verse.why: Even the strongest people freeze; the Gita begins with a breakdown, not a hero.
verse.misuse: Not a dismissal of anxiety; it shows that even the strong feel it, and the teaching starts there.

prasang.title: Overcome by delusion, Arjuna speaks in fear, love and grief
prasang.summary: Seeing his kin ready to die, Arjuna trembles, his bow slips, and he argues that no victory is worth killing family. He sits down in the chariot and refuses to fight.
prasang.story_hook: The greatest archer of his age stood between two armies, and his hands began to shake.
prasang.lesson: Even the strongest people freeze; the Gita begins with a breakdown, not a hero.

verse.meaning: Arjuna stands in his chariot on the battlefield and looks at the two armies. He sees his grand-uncle, his teachers, his cousins, and his friends lined up against him. The sight hits him like a physical blow. His limbs shake, his mouth goes dry, and his body trembles. He drops his bow and tells Krishna that he would rather die than kill the people he loves. The Gita opens with a breakdown, not a hero.
verse.for_you: You are in the middle of the night fights with your father. The Gita says even the strongest people freeze first. That is what is happening to you right now.

verse.speaker: Bhartrihari
verse.setting: From the section on wealth: how need changes what we value.
verse.sanskrit: परिक्षीणः कश्चित्स्पृहयति यवानां प्रसृतये स पश्चात् सम्पूर्णः कलयति धरित्रीं तृणसमाम् । अतश्चानैकान्त्याद्गुरुलघुतयाऽर्थेषु धनिना- मवस्था वस्तूनि प्रथयति च सङ्कोचयति च ॥
verse.line: Starving, a handful of grain is everything. Full, the whole earth looks like straw.
verse.translation: A man who has lost everything longs for a handful of barley; later, when full, he counts the whole earth as straw. Because nothing is fixed, a person's condition makes things look great or small.
verse.why: Money changes how others see you, not who you are. Give it, enjoy it, or lose it.

prasang.title: Nitishatakam: On wealth
prasang.summary: A wry look at money: how the world flatters the rich and forgets the broke, wealth's three destinies, and how distance and neglect ruin what we value. It closes with advice to the chataka bird not to plead before every cloud.
prasang.lesson: Money changes how others see you, not who you are. Give it, enjoy it, or lose it.

verse.meaning: You are in the middle of a fight that has no winner. Your father dismisses films as for rich kids and your mother cries in the kitchen. You lost your temper and regret it. The fight is not about the future or the money. It is about waiting for him to say it is enough. When we are empty inside, a handful of his approval feels like everything. When he is full of his own ideas, your whole life looks like straw to him.
verse.for_you: You are waiting for his nod to feel real. Today, notice when the wanting for it shows up in your chest. You do not need his stamp to know your path is real. You already know it.

verse.speaker: Bhartrihari
verse.sanskrit: निन्दन्तु नीतिनिपुणा यदि वा स्तुवन्तु लक्ष्मीः समाविशतु गच्छतु वा यथेष्टम् । अद्यैव वा मरणमस्तु युगान्तरे वा न्याय्यात्पथः प्रविचलन्ति पदं न धीराः ॥
verse.line: Let them praise or blame, let money come or go: the steady don't step off the right path.
verse.translation: Let the worldly-wise blame or praise; let fortune come or go as she pleases; let death come today or ages hence: the steadfast do not move a step from the path of what is right.
verse.why: Setbacks rarely last for those who keep going on the right path.

prasang.title: Nitishatakam: On steadfastness
prasang.summary: Steadfastness: the gods kept churning the ocean past jewels and poison until they found nectar; the steady do not leave the right path whatever people say. A struck ball bounces back and a cut tree grows again.
prasang.lesson: Setbacks rarely last for those who keep going on the right path.

verse.meaning: Bhartrihari says that the steady person does not leave the right path. They do not care if others praise them or blame them. They do not care if money comes or goes. They do not even care if death comes today or ages from now. They simply keep walking the path that is right for them.
verse.for_you: Your father's words are just noise. They cannot take the work you are doing. Keep walking your path, and let his praise or blame pass by you.

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna to Arjuna, describing the qualities of the person dear to God.
verse.sanskrit: तुल्यनिन्दास्तुतिर्मौनी सन्तुष्टो येनकेनचित् । अनिकेतः स्थिरमतिर्भक्तिमान्मे प्रियो नरः ॥
verse.line: Praise and blame weigh the same. Quiet, content with what comes, rooted in steadiness, not status.
verse.translation: to whom blame and praise are equal, who is silent, content with whatever comes, without a fixed home, steady in mind and full of devotion, that person is dear to me.
verse.why: Kindness without hatred, steadiness in praise and blame: that's what's loved.
verse.misuse: Not 'never ask for credit'. You can advocate for yourself without letting praise or blame define you.

prasang.title: The marks of one dear to God
prasang.summary: Krishna lists the marks of one dear to him: no hatred, friendly and compassionate, forgiving, content, disturbing no one and disturbed by no one, the same in praise and blame.
prasang.lesson: Kindness without hatred, steadiness in praise and blame: that's what's loved.

verse.meaning: Krishna is telling Arjuna what a person dear to God is like. It is a list of marks. The person does not hate. They are friendly and kind, and they forgive. They are content with what comes. They do not disturb anyone, and they are not disturbed by anyone. They are the same in praise and blame. They do not cling to a fixed home, but they are steady in their mind and full of devotion. That is the person who is loved.
verse.for_you: Your father calls your films for rich kids. His words sting. But your worth is not in his praise or blame. You can hold your love for him and keep your own steady ground. His approval is not the measure of who you are.

verse.speaker: Hanuman
verse.setting: Ram's advisers debate whether to trust Vibhishana; Hanuman gives his view.
verse.sanskrit: न वादान्नापि संघर्षानाधिक्यान च कामतः। वक्ष्यामि वचनं राजन्यथार्थं राम गौरवात्॥
verse.line: Speak not to win, compete or show off, but because the matter needs saying.
verse.translation: I will speak, king, not to argue, not to compete, not to show I know more, and not from my own wishes, but plainly, as the matter deserves, out of respect for you.
verse.why: Give a second chance to someone who comes to you sincerely, even across old lines.

prasang.title: Ram takes in the enemy's brother
prasang.summary: Vibhishana arrives at Ram's camp. The allies suspect a spy; Hanuman reads him as sincere. Ram decides: he will not turn away anyone who comes in friendship, even with faults; whoever comes once and says 'I am yours' he will protect.
prasang.story_hook: The enemy king's own brother was standing at the edge of the camp, asking to come in.
prasang.lesson: Give a second chance to someone who comes to you sincerely, even across old lines.

verse.meaning: Hanuman speaks to Ram after Vibhishana, the enemy's brother, arrives at the camp. The advisers think Vibhishana is a spy. Hanuman says he is not there to argue or win, but because the truth of the moment needs saying. He asks Ram to give Vibhishana a chance, even though he is from the other side. The verse says you could speak a hard truth not to defeat someone, but because the situation itself asks for it.
verse.for_you: Your father dismisses your films. You can tell him what you need without trying to win the argument tonight. Speak the truth, then stop. Let the silence hold the rest.

verse.speaker: Vidula
verse.setting: Queen Vidula rouses her son, who lies defeated and despairing after losing his kingdom.
verse.sanskrit: माऽऽत्मानमवमन्यस्व मैनमल्पेन बीभरः / मनः कृत्वा सुकल्याणं मा भैस्त्वं प्रतिसंहर
verse.line: Don't think less of yourself or settle for little. Set your mind on something good, and stop fearing.
verse.translation: Do not hold yourself in contempt, and do not keep it going on too little. Set your mind on what is truly good; don't be afraid. Pull yourself together.
verse.why: Past failure doesn't define you. Results are uncertain, but those who never try never succeed.

prasang.title: Vidula rouses her defeated son
prasang.summary: Kunti sends Yudhishthira the old story of Queen Vidula, who finds her son lying defeated after losing his kingdom. She shames, then reasons, then encourages him until he rises and fights for it again.
prasang.story_hook: A prince lay in bed after losing everything, until his mother walked in and refused to let him stay there.
prasang.lesson: Past failure doesn't define you. Results are uncertain, but those who never try never succeed.

verse.meaning: Queen Vidula finds her son Sanjaya lying defeated and despairing after losing his kingdom. She tells him to stop thinking less of himself and to stop settling for little. She says to set his mind on what is truly good and to stop fearing. She is telling him that past failure does not define him. Results are uncertain, but those who never try never succeed. You are not your worst night.
verse.for_you: Tonight, try one conversation with your father where you speak your truth and ask to be seen, without trying to win him over. Tell him what you feel, then step back.

story.title: The three boons and the refused fortune
story.story_hook: Death came home to find a boy who had waited three days on his doorstep without food.
story.summary: Death, away from home, keeps the boy waiting three days and offers three boons in apology. Nachiketa asks first that his father be calm and not angry with him, then for a sacred fire, then for the truth about death. Yama tempts him with sons, gold, long life and pleasures instead; the boy refuses them all.
story.lesson: Ask for peace with your family first, and don't trade the real question for comfort.

anchor.setting: Nachiketa's first boon: that his father be at peace and not angry with him.
anchor.sanskrit: यथा पुरस्ताद्भविता प्रतीत औद्दालकिरारुणिर्मत्प्रसृष्टः । सुखं रात्रीः शयिता वीतमन्युस्त्वां ददृशिवान्मृत्युमुखात्प्रमुक्तम् ॥
anchor.line: Your father will know you again, sleep well at night, his anger gone, when he sees you home.
anchor.translation: Your father, Auddalaki Aruni, will know you as before, by my leave. He will sleep peacefully at night, his anger gone, when he sees you released from the jaws of death.
anchor.why: Ask for peace with your family first, and don't trade the real question for comfort.

story.hook_title: Young Nachiketa waited three days at Death's door, and Death said sorry
story.teaser: Young Nachiketa waited three days at Death's door, and Death said sorry
story.for_you: Nachiketa stood before Yama and refused the easy gold, choosing the hard truth instead. You have refused to settle for your father's anger or your mother's tears.

script: The waiting after the fight is the heaviest part. You sit in your room and replay the words. You want your father to see what you are becoming. Instead, he calls your dreams a rich kid's game. You feel torn and unseen, like the love you share is trapped under a heavy lid.

Arjuna stands in his chariot on the battlefield. He looks across the field. He sees his grand-uncle, his teachers, and his cousins. They are lined up against him. The sight hits him like a physical blow. His limbs shake, his mouth goes dry, and his body trembles. He drops his bow and tells Krishna that he would rather die than kill the people he loves. Arjuna said:
सीदन्ति मम गात्राणि मुखं च परिशुष्यति, वेपथुश्च शरीरे मे रोमहर्षश्च जायते. गाण्डीवं स्रंसते हस्तात्त्वक्चैव परिदह्यते, न च शक्नोम्यवस्थातुं भ्रमतीव च मे मनः.
In plain words: Shaking limbs, a dry mouth, a racing body: the Gita opens with a panic attack, not a hero.

The Gita opens with a panic attack, not a hero. Even the strongest people freeze first. It is not a dismissal of anxiety. It is the truth underneath. The fight every night is what the Gita calls wanting your own way and then being angry when it does not happen. The love is real, but the wanting is what keeps it burning. This is easier said than done, because your heart is still with your father.

Tonight, when the room is quiet, notice the physical feeling. Is your mouth dry or your body trembling? That is not weakness. That is your body telling you that the love and the fight are two different things. You do not have to win the argument to be seen.
Can you hold the love and the fight in the same breath?

depth.life: You are in the middle of the night fights with your father, and you feel completely torn and unseen. You want his love but he only dismisses your world. You are waiting for him to say you are enough, and you are tired of the fighting.
depth.points: The Gita says even the strongest people freeze first, before they act. Your body knows the love is real and the pain is real. But the panic is what keeps you stuck in the same loop of wanting and fighting.
depth.practice: Sit with your hands on your knees for one minute. Notice where the fight is in your body without trying to fix it.
depth.question: What is your body trying to tell you when the fight starts?
